In six-dimensional [[geometry]], a '''truncated 6-cube''' (or '''truncated hexeract''') is a convex [[uniform 6-polytope]], being a [[Truncation (geometry)|truncation]] of the regular [[6-cube]].

There are 5 truncations for the 6-cube. Vertices of the truncated 6-cube are located as pairs on the edge of the 6-cube. Vertices of the bitruncated 6-cube are located on the square faces of the 6-cube. Vertices of the tritruncated 6-cube are located inside the [[cube|cubic]] cells of the 6-cube.

=== Alternate names ===
* Truncated hexeract (Acronym: tox) (Jonathan Bowers){{sfn|Klitzing|at=[https://bendwavy.org/klitzing/incmats/tox.htm (o3o3o3o3x4x - tox)]}}

=== Construction and coordinates ===
The truncated 6-cube may be constructed by [[Truncation (geometry)|truncating]] the vertices of the [[6-cube]] at <math>1/(\sqrt{2}+2)</math> of the edge length. A regular [[5-simplex]] replaces each original vertex.

The [[Cartesian coordinate]]s of the vertices of a ''truncated 6-cube'' having edge length&nbsp;2 are the permutations of:

:<math>\left(\pm1,\ \pm(1+\sqrt{2}),\ \pm(1+\sqrt{2}),\ \pm(1+\sqrt{2}),\ \pm(1+\sqrt{2}),\ \pm(1+\sqrt{2})\right)</math>

=== Alternate names ===
* Bitruncated hexeract (Acronym: botox) (Jonathan Bowers){{sfn|Klitzing|at=[https://bendwavy.org/klitzing/incmats/botox.htm (o3o3o3x3x4o - botox)]}}

=== Construction and coordinates ===
The [[Cartesian coordinate]]s of the vertices of a ''bitruncated 6-cube'' having edge length&nbsp;2 are the permutations of:
:<math>\left(0,\ \pm1,\ \pm2,\ \pm2,\ \pm2,\ \pm2 \right)</math>
